title: Governance and Human Oversight
tagline: Someone must be accountable, and the record must show it.
story: The agent has acted. A customer, an auditor or a regulator will ask who allowed it, who could have stopped it and how you found out. Here you decide how much human oversight each action deserves, which dated rules and frameworks apply, how a fleet of agents is inventoried and retired, and what you do when something goes wrong.
oneLiner: Match oversight to action risk and reversibility, then prove it with owners, records and a rehearsed incident process.
youWillLearn: Choose between approve, two-person review, escalate, sampled review and log-only oversight by flipping reversibility, reach, volume and regulatory class
Date the EU AI Act obligations correctly, including the 2026 Digital Omnibus changes, and say which apply to an assistant
Compare the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF with its GenAI profile, ISO/IEC 42001 and the Microsoft Responsible AI Standard by what each is and is not
Run an agent lifecycle from inventory to retirement, with Microsoft Agent 365 and Entra Agent ID as the Microsoft stack options
Plan AI incident response with staged containment, the right records and the Article 73 deadlines
Defend a governance programme for a fleet of agents

flashcards.front: Name the oversight patterns and the trigger for each.
flashcards.back: Approve before action (irreversible or externally visible), two-person review (highest risk), escalate on a trigger (low confidence or policy hit), sampled review with undo (high volume, reversible), log and alert only (low risk).

flashcards.front: What does EU AI Act Article 14 expect of human oversight for high-risk systems?
flashcards.back: Measures proportionate to risk, autonomy and context. People can understand limits, stay aware of automation bias, interpret output, decide not to use or override it, and interrupt with a stop control.

flashcards.front: When do Annex III high-risk rules apply after the Digital Omnibus?
flashcards.back: 2027-12-02. Annex I product-embedded systems follow on 2028-08-02. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 was published 2026-07-24 and entered into force 2026-07-27. Posts that say 2026-08-02 are out of date.

flashcards.front: What began on 2026-08-02 under the EU AI Act?
flashcards.back: Article 50 transparency rules apply, and enforcement starts for GPAI obligations, prohibitions, transparency and AI literacy. Systems on the market before that date have until 2026-12-02 for Article 50(2) marking.

flashcards.front: EU AI Act maximum fines under Article 99?
flashcards.back: Prohibited practices: EUR 35M or 7% of worldwide turnover. Other operator obligations: EUR 15M or 3%. Incorrect information: EUR 7.5M or 1%. Undertakings pay the higher figure, SMEs the lower (small mid-caps too on the 3% and 1% tiers).

flashcards.front: Serious incident reporting deadlines for high-risk systems (Article 73)?
flashcards.back: No later than 15 days after becoming aware, 2 days for widespread infringements or Article 3(49)(b) incidents, and 10 days after a death. An initial incomplete report is allowed.

flashcards.front: What is the NIST AI RMF, and how is the GenAI profile related?
flashcards.back: A voluntary framework (1.0 released 2023-01-26, under revision) with four functions: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage. NIST AI 600-1 (2024-07-26) is the GenAI profile with twelve risks.
An organization's AI management system (AIMS), run as Plan-Do-Check-Act. Published December 2023 and certifiable. It does not certify one application's behaviour.

flashcards.front: What is in the Microsoft Responsible AI Standard v2?
flashcards.back: A June 2022 external release with six goal groups: accountability, transparency, fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness. It includes goal A5 human oversight and control and a Sensitive Uses review at least annually.

flashcards.front: List the agent governance lifecycle stages.
flashcards.back: Inventory, identity, permissions, review, retirement. An agent that is not in the inventory has no sponsor, no review date and no retirement path.
A control plane to observe, govern and secure agents through a registry, Entra, Purview and Defender. Generally available 2026-05-01 for the Commercial segment, licensed per user.

flashcards.front: Entra Agent ID: sponsor versus owner?
flashcards.back: Sponsors are business representatives, at least one required, accountable for purpose and lifecycle. They can disable or soft-delete but not edit auth. Owners are optional technical admins who manage credentials and can re-enable or hard-delete.

flashcards.front: How are agents governed when they cannot do MFA?
flashcards.back: With Conditional Access, evaluated when a token is issued or refreshed, and ID Governance access packages for agent identities. Licensing requirements apply.

flashcards.front: How does Microsoft Agent Framework gate a tool call on a human?
flashcards.back: Python: `@tool(approval_mode="always_require")` and check `result.user_input_requests`. .NET: wrap the function in `ApprovalRequiredAIFunction`. Approvals bind to a pending request in the same session by default.

flashcards.front: Microsoft's three stages of AI incident remediation?
flashcards.back: Contain in the first hour, expand and strengthen mitigations in the first 24 hours, fix at source over days or weeks. Add watch periods after each stage because behaviour is non-deterministic.

flashcards.front: Why is AI incident severity hard to rank?
flashcards.back: Severity depends on domain, affected people and content, not record count. Root cause can span data, fine-tuning, retrieval and context, and standard telemetry misses output anomalies.

flashcards.front: What does Article 50(1) require of AI systems that interact with people?
flashcards.back: Providers must design them so people are told they are interacting with an AI system, unless that is obvious from context. The information must be clear at the latest at the first interaction.

flashcards.front: What must high-risk systems record under Article 12?
flashcards.back: Automatic recording of events (logs) over the system's lifetime, enough for risk identification, post-market monitoring and monitoring of operation.

glossary.def: A person approves or decides before the system acts. The strongest brake and the most friction.
A person monitors and can intervene, but the system acts without waiting. Sampled review and alerting sit here.
The tendency to over-trust system output. Article 14 expects overseers to stay aware of it.
Approvals given without real review because volume, time pressure or a bare yes or no screen makes careful review impossible.
How cheaply an action can be undone. The first dial for choosing the oversight level.
EU AI Act roles. A provider develops or places an AI system on the market. A deployer uses it under its own authority. Duties differ by role.
An AI system in an Annex III use area or an Annex I product. Its core duties apply from 2027-12-02 and 2028-08-02 after the Digital Omnibus.
AI management system, the organization-wide system that ISO/IEC 42001 specifies and certifies.
The business representative accountable for an agent's purpose and lifecycle in Entra Agent ID. At least one is required.
The inventory of agents with owners, identities and status. In Agent 365 it lives in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
A Microsoft Responsible AI Standard review for uses with a higher risk of harm, repeated at least annually.
An incident of a high-risk system that the EU AI Act requires its provider to report to market surveillance authorities within the Article 73 deadlines of 15, 2 or 10 days.

claims.text: The EU AI Act entered into force on 2024-08-01, prohibitions and AI literacy apply from 2025-02-02 and general-purpose AI obligations from 2025-08-02.
From 2026-08-02 the Article 50 transparency rules apply and enforcement starts for GPAI, prohibitions, transparency and AI literacy.
On 2026-12-02 new prohibitions apply and the Article 50(2) transition for systems already on the market ends.
The AI Omnibus moves Annex III high-risk rules to 2027-12-02 and Annex I rules to 2028-08-02.
Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) was signed on 2026-07-08, published in the Official Journal on 2026-07-24 and entered into force on 2026-07-27.

The AI Omnibus extends SME relief to small mid-caps, simplifies AI literacy, prohibits AI that generates non-consensual sexual content or child sexual abuse material, and allows special-category data processing to detect and correct bias.
AI systems placed on the market before 2026-08-02 have until 2026-12-02 to comply with Article 50(2) machine-readable marking.

Article 99 fines: prohibited practices up to EUR 35,000,000 or 7% of worldwide annual turnover, other operator obligations up to EUR 15,000,000 or 3%, incorrect information up to EUR 7,500,000 or 1%. Undertakings pay the higher figure, SMEs the lower, and small mid-caps the lower figure for the 3% and 1% tiers.

Article 14 expects oversight proportionate to risk, awareness of automation bias, the ability to override and a stop control, and two competent persons verifying separately for Annex III point 1(a) biometric identification.

Article 50(1) requires providers to design systems so people are told they interact with an AI system, 50(2) requires machine-readable marking of synthetic content, and 50(4) requires deployers to disclose deep fakes and public-interest text unless human-reviewed.

Article 73 requires serious incident reports within 15 days of awareness, within 2 days for a widespread infringement or an Article 3(49)(b) incident, and within 10 days after a death. An incomplete initial report is allowed.
Article 12 requires high-risk systems to allow automatic recording of events over their lifetime for risk identification, post-market monitoring and monitoring of operation.
The GPAI Code of Practice was published on 2025-07-10, is voluntary and has Transparency, Copyright and Safety and Security chapters. Safety and Security covers Article 55 for systemic-risk models.
NIST AI RMF 1.0 was released on 2023-01-26 with the functions Govern, Map, Measure and Manage, and NIST says it is being revised.
NIST AI 600-1, the Generative AI Profile, was released on 2024-07-26 and lists twelve risks, with prompt injection and data poisoning under information security.
ISO/IEC 42001:2023 is a certifiable AI management system standard run as Plan-Do-Check-Act, published in December 2023, and governs an organization's AI practice, not one application.
The Microsoft Responsible AI Standard v2 (June 2022) has six goal groups, includes goal A5 human oversight and control and a Sensitive Uses review repeated at least annually.
Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management for AI is the entry point for visibility into AI usage.

Defender for Cloud AI threat protection is GA, alerts on data leakage, data poisoning, jailbreak and credential theft, covers Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Model Inference with text tokens only, and is available in the commercial cloud only.
In Microsoft Agent Framework Python a tool uses @tool(approval_mode="always_require") and the run result exposes user_input_requests. In .NET the function is wrapped in ApprovalRequiredAIFunction.

By default a local approval response authorizes a tool call only when it matches a pending approval request in the same AgentSession. disable_approval_response_binding opts out and can let a fabricated or replayed response approve a privileged call.
Microsoft Agent 365 was generally available from 2026-05-01 for the Commercial segment on a per-user basis, with Microsoft E5 as the best-fit prerequisite.
Agent 365 observes, governs and secures agents through a registry in the Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft Entra, Microsoft Purview and Microsoft Defender.
The Agent 365 registry has four types: Microsoft agents, external partner-built agents, published by your org, and shared by creator.
Entra Agent ID requires at least one sponsor per agent identity and blueprint. Sponsors can disable or soft-delete, and owners are optional and can also re-enable, restore and hard-delete.
Agents have no MFA and are governed with Conditional Access, which needs Microsoft 365 E7 or an Agent 365 licence with at least Entra P1 or Microsoft 365 E3.

An Entra agent identity is a service principal with servicePrincipalType ServiceIdentity and holds no credentials of its own. The blueprint holds credentials. Execution modes are S2S, OBO and Agentic-User, and Agentic-User needs the Frontier preview program.

Microsoft's AI incident response guidance names taxonomy gaps, context-dependent severity, ambiguous root cause and telemetry gaps, and prescribes containment in the first hour, expansion in the first 24 hours and a fix at source over days or weeks.
At the Agent 365 general availability announcement on 2026-05-01, discovery of local and shadow agents through Defender and Intune was announced as preview.

Meta's Agents Rule of Two (2025-10-31) says to require human approval or an equivalent when a session needs untrustworthy input, sensitive access and the ability to change state or communicate externally.
